<title id="title">Coffee bean cup cosy — gauge-correct knitting chart</title><desc id="desc">A 60 stitch by 24 round stranded knitting chart with three chocolate coffee beans on a cream background. <text x="516" y="773" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="600" fill="#35261f" >1 cell = 1 stitch × 1 round</text>
<text x="516" y="797" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="14" font-weight="400" fill="#756557" >Read bottom to top; every round runs right → left. Knit all chart stitches.</text>
<text x="64" y="855" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#885a3c" letter-spacing="1.3">02  /  KNIT THE SLEEVE</text>
<text x="64" y="882" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="400" fill="#35261f" >Cast on 60 sts in MC. Join without twisting; place a marker.</text>
<text x="64" y="907" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="400" fill="#35261f" >Work 3 rounds of k1, p1 rib. Work chart rounds 1–24 once.</text>
<text x="64" y="932" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="400" fill="#35261f" >Finish with 3 rounds of k1, p1 rib in MC; bind off loosely.</text>
<text x="64" y="957" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="400" fill="#35261f" >Weave in ends and block to gauge. Try on your cup for fit.</text>
<text x="672" y="855" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12" font-weight="700" fill="#885a3c" letter-spacing="1.3">03  /  WHY THE CELLS ARE WIDE</text>
<text x="672" y="882" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="400" fill="#35261f" >At this gauge, a stitch is 4.17 mm wide × 3.13 mm tall.</text>
<text x="672" y="907" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="400" fill="#35261f" >Cells use that 4:3 ratio, so the beans keep their shape.</text>
<text x="672" y="932" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="400" fill="#35261f" >Swatch first; a different gauge can distort the motif.</text>
<text x="672" y="957" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="400" fill="#35261f" >Catch long floats every 3–4 sts; keep the fabric relaxed.</text>
